# Trellis AI guidance for TypeScript services

Last verified against Trellis main (2026-08-29).

Use this file for AI coding agents working in a TypeScript service repository
that consumes Trellis. The language-neutral guide is:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qlever-llc/trellis/main/docs/static/llms-full.txt

For Svelte browser apps, use:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qlever-llc/trellis/main/docs/static/llms-svelte.txt

## Service repository setup

- Manage local or OCI canonical API dependencies with `trellis add`, `trellis rm`,
  `trellis update`, and lock-stable `trellis install`. Commit `trellis.toml` and
  `trellis.lock`, ignore `.trellis/`, link
  `.trellis/generated/ts/trellis-apis` in Deno, and import stable subpaths such
  as `@trellis/apis/acme.orders`. Install verifies exact API ID, release, and
  semantic digest, and remote OCI digest and never executes provider source.

Recommended TypeScript service shape:

```text
services/<name>/
|-- deno.json or package.json
|-- contract.ts              # Single-contract public entrypoint
|-- contracts/*.ts           # Optional multi-contract modules
|-- schemas/*.ts             # TypeBox wire schemas and exported model schemas
|-- errors/*.ts              # Service-local transportable errors
|-- rpc/*.ts                 # RPC handlers
|-- events/*.ts              # Event listeners and publishers
|-- operations/*.ts          # Operation providers
|-- db/ and migrations/      # Service-local storage and migrations
|-- config.ts                # Zod environment/config parsing
`-- main.ts                  # Bootstrap, registration, shutdown
```

Rules:

- single-contract services normally expose `contract.ts`; multi-contract services
  may use `contracts/*.ts` and optionally re-export the primary default contract
  from `contract.ts`
- every TypeScript contract source loaded by Trellis generation should
  default-export the `defineServiceContract(...)`, `defineAppContract(...)`,
  `defineAgentContract(...)`, or `defineDeviceContract(...)` result
- every `define*Contract` body requires `id` (stable participant identity),
  `apiId` (owned API identity), and `apiVersion` (Semantic Version release
  metadata), even when the identities are equal. Release version does not affect
  the semantic API digest, participant evidence, permissions, or subjects.
- import those normal contract helpers from the browser-safe
  `@qlever-llc/trellis` root. Keep service runtime, device activation,
  browser-auth, telemetry, generated SDK, and advanced contract tooling imports on
  their explicit subpaths.
- Browser apps use `TrellisClient.connect(...)` as the sole auth lifecycle owner.
  Do not start or bind flows, persist auth state, or classify auth messages in UI
  wrappers. Browser bundles require `nats.transports.websocket`; service and Deno
  device runtimes require `nats.transports.native`. Refresh installs the complete
  returned session, JWT, transport, clock, and authorization-context bundle.
- Device activation wait repeats `/bootstrap/device` with a fresh proof over the
  same target session identity and uses
  `expiresAt - serverNow` as a monotonic duration. A changed review id is an
  explicit expired/replaced review, not a review to follow silently. Resolve
  cancellation is unsupported.
- `deno.json` should expose locked API installation through `trellis install`
- Contract resolution must be deterministic from tracked source. Undeclared
  time, randomness, network, environment, and external-file inputs are unsupported.
- service-boundary integration tests can use
  `@qlever-llc/trellis-test/integration` and
  `@qlever-llc/trellis-test/integration/runner`: define
  `trellis.integration.ts` with an explicit `runtime.trellis.command`,
  `denoTestArgs`, and case descriptors; use `trellisIntegrationTest(...)`,
  `runtimeScopeForCase(CASE_ID)`, fixed authored contract ids/actions/subjects,
  case-slugged physical names and state/resource keys, contract approval/provisioning,
  `TrellisService.connect(...)`, `runtime.connectClient(...)`, and
  `runtime.captureEvents(...)` when needed. Run isolated cases with `--config`;
  use shared mode with `--parallel --jobs 1`. Shared cases use one NATS account,
  Trellis process, and SQLite set; the harness resets stale accepted authority
  before attached authentication. Higher worker counts are rejected because
  fixed protocol subjects share that account. `trellis-test` runs NATS as a managed child process from pinned,
  checksum-verified nats-server and nsc binaries (cached under
  `TRELLIS_TEST_CACHE_DIR`, default `~/.cache/trellis-test`; first use downloads them, requiring network; every reuse revalidates the cached archive sha256 against the pin and byte-checks the cached binary against a fresh extraction, so corrupted or replaced cache entries are reinstalled, and and `sh` must be on `PATH`); no container runtime is
  required.
- The `trellis` CLI runs the runtime with
  `trellis server [mode] --config PATH [--nats URL | --nats-binary PATH]
  [--nats-state-dir PATH] [--check]` (mode defaults to `all`; `--check`
  validates configuration, trust, stores, streams, and NATS connectivity,
  then exits). Managed mode (no `--nats`) downloads the pinned nats-server
  release, verifies its checksum, caches it under `TRELLIS_CACHE_DIR`
  (default `~/.cache/trellis`), listens on 127.0.0.1 ports 4222 (NATS), 8222
  (monitoring), and 8080 (websocket), and stops the server when the CLI
  exits. `--nats URL` runs against an external server; `--nats-binary PATH`
  manages an existing trusted nats-server binary without re-verifying it;
  `--nats-state-dir PATH` keeps all mutable managed-NATS files (rendered
  configs, pid file, resolver JWTs, JetStream data) outside a read-only
  bundle.
- The runtime OCI image bakes the `trellis` CLI and the pinned,
  checksum-verified nats-server at `/usr/local/bin/nats-server`; `nsc` is
  test-harness-only and not in the image. The entrypoint stays
  `trellis-server` for external-NATS deployments. For a managed single
  container, mount the generated bundle read-only from its own named volume
  and the writable state on a second volume
  (`trellis-bundle:/etc/trellis:ro,Z`, `trellis-state:/var/lib/trellis:rw,Z`),
  with the bundle's SQLite store paths rewritten to the state volume, and run
  `trellis server ... --nats-binary /usr/local/bin/nats-server
  --nats-state-dir /var/lib/trellis/nats`.
- commit `trellis.toml` and `trellis.lock`, then run `trellis install` to
  materialize locked APIs and consumer-local SDKs
- generated SDKs, manifests, and package outputs belong under the service repo's
  generated output locations; do not edit generated files by hand
- public contract object schemas are open by default; use `Type.Object({ ... })`
  without `additionalProperties: false` unless a security-sensitive proof
  boundary or another documented requirement must reject unknown fields
- after changing a contract, run `trellis install` before typing extracted
  handlers so generated SDK aliases match the current surfaces
- App and device contracts may declare schema-backed value or map State stores and
  use their generated `client.state.<store>` facades. State supports revisions,
  per-entry TTL, and author-declared migration versions; services use
  `service.kv`, and callers never access the internal `trellis_state` bucket.
- TypeScript contract authoring compiles to canonical `trellis.api.v1` and
  `trellis.participant.v1` artifacts before bootstrap. Do not send legacy contract
  manifests directly to the Rust auth runtime.
- HTTP is limited to browser/account flows, initial service/device bootstrap,
  proof-bound restart recovery, and portal assets. Connected control,
  including auth control, uses generated APIs over NATS; do not add HTTP
  context, revocation, logout, or client-bootstrap calls.
- `TrellisService.connect(...)`, `TrellisClient.connect(...)`, and device helpers
  own session bootstrap and reconnect. They use an immutable provisioned identity
  or browser session key, a session-bound deny-all JWT, the standard NATS nonce
  signature, and a digest-only context token. Ready bootstrap includes a pinned trust root and
  signed short-lived context. TypeScript delegates cryptographic verification to
  the Rust/WASM verifier. Production service/device clients must provide a
  durable authorization-context store; browser clients use origin-scoped
  IndexedDB, while memory is explicit for tests and ephemeral processes. Stores
  atomically retain the root key id/digest, minimum manifest generation/digest,
  and current context across restarts. A newer `manifest.current` is persisted
  before stale context is cleared and the existing refresh task is woken.
  Clearing context retains trust. Clients
  accept issuer overlap only through direct public-key entries in the exact
  accepted manifest generation. Clients compute deterministic refresh time and atomically use the
  current digest on reconnect. Bootstrap/refresh server time is converted to a
  request-midpoint clock offset. Context refresh is restart recovery and returns
  route/session/NATS metadata with the renewed route credential and context.
  After context or route-JWT expiry, clients retain session/trust evidence and
  use proof-bound `currentContextDigest: null` recovery; same-digest success
  still reschedules. Pending devices retry `/bootstrap/device`.
  Rust/WASM is authoritative for TypeScript security-object verification.
  Provider authorization state uses
  the internal NATS KV registry with readiness, manifest/revocation watches, and
  reconnect reconstruction; registry handles are not service-author APIs and
  ordinary cache hits perform no external I/O. Each verified context remains an
  opaque Rust/WASM handle reused for request and event proofs, then is discarded
  on manifest-epoch change. Quiet watches remain healthy.
  Native Deno/Node services can use `FileAuthorizationContextStore` from the
  explicit `@qlever-llc/trellis/auth/file` subpath; it is intentionally absent
  from the browser-safe auth graph. Each file path is single-writer and must be
  private to one active service/client process.
  Service/device bootstrap presents canonical participant and referenced API
  artifacts inside the signed request. Service repositories do not load shared
  NATS credentials or authorization registry KV directly.
- Every RPC request and published event carries a context-bound v2 proof. The
  receiving provider verifies requests locally from its in-memory authorization
  cache, and runtime event consumers verify events locally against retained
  historical evidence. There is no central Auth validation RPC on either hot
  path; do not add one or perform provider-side session database lookups solely
  for authorization.
- Ordinary context expiry still permits delayed historical event verification;
  explicit context revocation invalidates every RPC and event proof from that
  context, including proofs created before revocation.
- The deny-all bootstrap JWT grants no authority. Context refresh is restart
  recovery: it renews the route credential and installs its exact expiry
  atomically with the verified context. It only routes Auth Callout and remains
  bounded by current session, authority, delegation, context, and the configured
  JWT lifetime cap.
- `maximumContextBytes` is the canonical complete signed-context JSON UTF-8 byte
  limit, not the base64url token length.
- Trellis caches manifests by digest at runtime. If auth/bootstrap reports a
  missing digest after the cache is pruned, regenerate from source and present the
  full source boundary so the client can recompile its protocol artifacts; do not
  patch deployment authority or implementation offers by hand.
- Deployment authority proposal/desired `needs` are grouped by `contracts`,
  `surfaces`, `capabilities`, and `resources`. Materialized authority is a
  projection with runtime `grants` grouped by `capabilities`, `surfaces`, and
  `nats`; service permissions require current materialization for the accepted
  desired authority version. Stale or obsolete persisted projections are repaired
  by Trellis storage upgrade and reconciliation.
- Deployment materialization is shared by the deployment and exact participant.
  Session and instance eligibility is checked separately, so one unhealthy
  instance does not rewrite authority for healthy peers.
- Additive compatible participant changes produce update proposals; incompatible
  API changes produce migration proposals. Equivalent retries reuse one semantic
  proposal, and changed proposals supersede older pending proposals. Each
  deployment + participant has one stable authority lineage; terminal plan
  history never blocks later reproposal.
- Deployment authority plans can be `superseded`; only `pending` plans targeting
  the current desired authority version are actionable.
- Deployment authority plans expose `breakingChanges` as structured per-target
  compatibility failures for operator UI.
- Portal helpers submit only the current server-owned consent digest, selected
  optional bundle ids, decision, and idempotency key. Do not send grants,
  capabilities, resource atoms, or expiry. OIDC callbacks are browser-cookie and
  portal-policy bound. The server-owned consent proposal is immutable across flow
  state transitions.
- Trusted portal policy is exact to portal + participant and may select only
  proposal-defined capabilities through base policy or verified provider-role
  mappings. Successful trusted local registration applies that policy immediately
  like local or OIDC login. On policy changes, Trellis revokes superseded contexts;
  removing a portal, provider allowance, or policy also clears verified-role
  provenance. Restoring configuration alone cannot replay cached roles: a new
  verified login is required. Retained sessions can refresh and reconnect after
  eligible authority returns.
- Treat bindings as physical evidence, never authority. Bootstrap replay
  revalidates current state and returns a newly generated credential.
- TypeScript telemetry helpers are exported from `@qlever-llc/trellis/telemetry`.
  Use `recordTrellisDuration(...)` for low-cardinality OpenTelemetry duration
  histograms and `recordTrellisError(...)` for error counters. Metric attributes
  must not include user IDs, session keys, flow IDs, request IDs, trace IDs,
  contract IDs, NATS subjects, URLs, or other unbounded values.

## Use surface-first APIs

Use generated facades on the connected client:

```ts
const order = await client.rpc.orders.get({ orderId: "ord_123" }).orThrow();

await client.event.orders.shipped.publish({
  orderId: "ord_123",
  customerId: "cust_456",
  shippedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
}).orThrow();

const feed = await client.feed.orders.live({ customerId: "cust_456" }).orThrow();

const op = await client.operation.orders.process
  .start({ orderId: "ord_123" })
  .orThrow();
```

An operation or job queue may declare one optional `update` schema. Keep
`progress` for low-frequency durable telemetry/snapshots. Updates are typed
live-only, at-most-once content: they are not persisted, replayed, exposed in
admin/Event Log, or delivered to late subscribers. Prefer cumulative payloads
and treat terminal output/result as authoritative.
Operation and job traffic remains bounded by transport permissions compiled from
the connected service context; declarations and subject names never create
grants.

```ts
// Inside an operation handler:
await op.emitUpdate({ completed: 3, total: 10 }).orThrow();

const ref = await client.operation.orders.process
  .input({ orderId: "ord_123" })
  .onUpdate((event) => console.log(event.update))
  .start()
  .orThrow();
const events = await ref.watch({ updates: true }).orThrow();

// Inside an active job handler:
await job.emitUpdate({ completed: 3, total: 10 }).orThrow();
const updates = await jobRef.updates().orThrow();
const early = await service.jobs.syncOrder.updates(preallocatedJobId).orThrow();
early.unsubscribe();
```

Job subscriptions filter stale attempts and duplicate or out-of-order
attempt-local sequences and clean up when iteration ends or `unsubscribe()` is
called. SQL-outbox callers should subscribe by the returned preallocated
`jobId` before dispatch when early frames matter. Job update subjects are
private Core NATS outside `JOBS`; application code must not build them.

Close or abort feed subscriptions when the caller no longer needs them. Trellis
propagates cancellation to the provider's `signal`; feed handlers must stop
connection-scoped work and release resources when that signal aborts.

If a generated facade is missing, check the contract generation path or the
current API reference.

For cross-contract calls, declare a narrow `uses` selection and call the other
contract SDK's `use(spec)` helper with only the blocks needed by this service.
Avoid broad selections just to make generated client types appear.

Connected TypeScript clients, devices, and services do not expose raw NATS
handles. Use generated `rpc`, `event`, `feed`, `operation`, `state`, and
`transfer` surfaces for communication, `service.kv` / `service.store` /
`service.jobs` for service-owned resources, and `connection` for lifecycle status
or shutdown.

Store and transfer bodies accept `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` and async iterables
for bounded streaming. Use `bytes()` only when intentionally collecting the whole
value in memory. Cancelling a receive stream sends an authenticated transfer
cancel control and waits for its acknowledgement; a caller may already have
consumed a valid prefix. Grants restrict frames to 1 byte through 1 MiB and
completed transfers require independent size and SHA-256 verification.

For browser app sign-out, use the connected generated Auth API over NATS. Do not
add an HTTP logout, context, revocation, or client-bootstrap call, and do not
hard-code IdP endpoints or arbitrary return URLs.

For user labels on records that already contain Trellis user ids, declare
`Auth.Users.Resolve` and pass the explicit ids. Do not request `Auth.Users.List`
or build app-local profile tables for basic display labels.

For integration tests, prefer `@qlever-llc/trellis-test/integration` over raw
NATS subjects or hand-built bootstrap responses. Serial runs isolate each
selected test with the `runtime` option passed to `trellisIntegrationTest(...)`,
usually imported from the same `trellis.integration.ts` module used by the runner
config. Shared runs use one NATS account, Trellis runtime, and SQLite set with one
worker. Keep authored contracts, actions, subjects, and participant identities
fixed; case-scope only physical deployments, resource keys, durable names, and
domain records. Configure runtime-wide authority-plan acceptance with the
top-level `authority.autoAccept` option. Allow migration plans only in tests that
intentionally cover migrations, using per-approval `allowPlanClassifications` or
explicit authority-plan helpers.

RPC handler `context.afterReply(task)` is only for effects that must run after a
successful response is published and flushed, such as disconnecting the caller.
Normal handler effects should complete before returning.
Use `runtime.connectClient(...)`, `runtime.captureEvents(...)`, and exported
assertion helpers for captured events, terminal jobs and operations, and
immediate or eventual `Result` RPC values.

Do not use fake NATS, fake Trellis runtimes, fake auth, fake generated clients,
or hand-built bootstrap/control-plane responders to prove Trellis behavior. If a
live integration test needs a missing failure or inspection surface, add the
smallest named test helper instead of enriching a fake.

For service-private jobs that must be singleton per logical key, declare
`keyConcurrency` on the job queue. Configure per-instance worker count on
`service.jobs.<queue>.handle(handler, { concurrency })`; it is not part of the
contract or resource binding. Keyed queues default to clear failure
(`stalePolicy: "fail-stale"`, `whenFull: "reject"`); only use
`whenFull: "coalesce"` or `"replace-oldest"` when the service explicitly wants
scheduler-style compression or supersession. `create(...)` means “create a new
job or return a typed failure”; use the additive `submit(...)` helper when code
needs to inspect accepted/rejected/coalesced/replaced outcomes.

Job handlers that need JetStream redelivery should return or throw
`RetryJobError` from `@qlever-llc/trellis/jobs`. Ordinary thrown errors or
`Result.err(...)` values remain terminal job failures.

For Jobs admin clients, use `Jobs.Query` for server-side search/sort/group/stats,
`Jobs.Metrics` for grouped operational summaries and time buckets, and
`Jobs.Inspect` for one-job detail, timeline, attempts, related jobs, errors,
trigger, lineage, and current `waitingOn` edges. Jobs remain `active` while
waiting. Trellis records `JobRef.wait()` and `OperationRef.wait()` automatically
inside active job handlers; wrap long external awaits with `job.waitFor(...)` and
safe metadata. `Jobs.List` and `Jobs.Get` are removed. Use `Jobs.Watch` as an
invalidation feed only; rerun the query, metrics, or inspection read after
invalidation frames. Admin mutations accept optional `reason`, and active
cancellation remains cooperative through `Jobs.Cancel`.

For Event Log admin clients, use the read-only `EventLog.Query`,
`EventLog.Inspect`, `EventLog.Metrics`, `EventLog.Consumers.Query`, and
`EventLog.Watch` surfaces. Event Log is optional observability infrastructure;
apps should declare it as an optional dependency unless they cannot operate
without historical event data. Treat publisher deployment as verified session
attribution, not subject inference; subject/catalog matching identifies owner
contract/event. `EventLog.Query` accepts `includeEventTypes` and
`excludeEventTypes` arrays of `{ ownerContractId, ownerEventName }` pairs and
`integrityExceptionOnly` for events whose owner resolution or proof verification
failed. `EventLog.Metrics` returns exact `summary.integrityExceptions`, resolved
event-type counts, and typed `buckets` with volume, payload size, resolution, and
verification counts.

## Register handlers with `service.handle`

Register providers through the generated `service.handle` tree. Handler code
receives typed input and a scoped `client` for allowed outbound calls. Trellis
does not provide application dependency injection; handler arguments contain only
Trellis-owned runtime data. Application resources are supplied by normal
JavaScript closure or factory patterns.

```ts
import { Result } from "@qlever-llc/trellis";

await service.handle.rpc.orders.get(async ({ input, client }) => {
  const row = await loadOrder(input.orderId);
  if (!row) return Result.err(orderNotFound(input.orderId));

  await client.event.orders.viewed.publish({
    orderId: input.orderId,
    viewedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
  }).orThrow();

  return Result.ok(row);
});
```

The scoped `client` represents the service's allowed outbound dependencies.
Register event listeners during service startup with `service.event`.

When handlers need application-owned dependencies, capture them in a closure:

```ts
import { Result } from "@qlever-llc/trellis";
import type { OrdersGetHandler } from "@my-org/orders-service-sdk";

const deps = { db, logger };

await service.handle.rpc.orders.get(async ({ input, client }) => {
  const row = await deps.db.orders.get(input.orderId);
  if (!row) return Result.err(orderNotFound(input.orderId));

  deps.logger.info({ orderId: input.orderId }, "loaded order");
  await client.event.orders.viewed.publish({ orderId: input.orderId }).orThrow();

  return Result.ok(row);
});

export const getOrder: OrdersGetHandler = async ({ input, client }) => {
  const row = await deps.db.orders.get(input.orderId);
  if (!row) return Result.err(orderNotFound(input.orderId));

  await client.event.orders.viewed.publish({ orderId: input.orderId }).orThrow();
  return Result.ok(row);
};
```

Inline handlers infer from the `service.handle...` registration site. Extracted
RPC, event, feed, operation, and job handlers should use concrete handler aliases
from the generated SDK, for example `OrdersGetHandler`.

## Schemas and errors

- Use TypeBox for contract wire schemas: RPC input/output, event payloads, feed
  input/events, operation input/output/progress, and resource declarations.
- Event subject `params` are JSON Pointers into the event payload. They must
  resolve to string, number, or integer-compatible schema nodes. For `anyOf` or
  `oneOf` event payload schemas, every branch must contain each routed pointer.
- Use Zod for environment and local configuration parsing.
- Use Trellis pagination helpers for list RPCs instead of inventing new page
  envelopes. Offset pagination uses `PageRequestSchema`,
  `PageResponseSchema(entry)`, `normalizePageQuery(...)`, and
  `buildPageResponse(...)`. Stable ID/keyset pagination uses `CursorQuerySchema`,
  `CursorPageSchema(item)`, `CursorPageResponseSchema<TItem>`,
  `normalizeCursorQuery(...)`, and `buildCursorPage(...)`.
- Use `withTrellisValidation(schema, extension)` from
  `@qlever-llc/trellis/contracts` to attach UI-facing `x-trellis-validation`
  metadata to TypeBox schema nodes. The metadata is purely for UX and does not
  change validation behavior.
- When every pre-handler schema validation failure is annotated, Trellis returns
  `SchemaValidationError` instead of `ValidationError` — the handler does not
  run in either case. `SchemaValidationError` carries an `issues[]` array with
  stable field-level UX information (path, keyword, code, message, label, note,
  severity, params). A single structural or unannotated failure downgrades the
  entire response to `ValidationError`.
- Return declared business errors through `Result` values. Use `.orThrow()` only
  at process boundaries where throwing is intentional.
- Extracted handler aliases accept source `defineError(...)` instances when their
  serialized data matches the generated declared error data. Client-side SDKs
  still reconstruct declared errors as generated SDK classes.

## Operation Typed Errors
- Operations support declared expected errors: `errors: [ref.error(...)]`
- Declared operation errors narrow `op.fail(error)` to the declared error union plus Trellis runtime errors
- Generated SDK types include `{Base}OperationHandlerError` aliases
- Manifest: operation descriptors carry `errors: [{ type: "..." }]`

## Prepared events and outbox/inbox

Trellis signs event publishes at publish time and consumers validate event proofs
before invoking handlers. Prepared events intentionally store subject, payload,
event id, and event time without deployment or contract metadata; runtime publish
adds proof headers from the current session.

Direct publish is the default when no local transaction must be coupled to the
event:

```ts
await client.event.orders.shipped.publish({
  orderId: input.orderId,
  customerId: input.customerId,
  shippedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
}).orThrow();
```

Generated SDK event types are event bodies. Trellis event metadata is assigned by
the runtime and is available as `PreparedTrellisEvent.header` after `prepare(...)`
and as `context.id` / `context.time` in event listeners.

For integration tests that must observe a published live event, start
`runtime.captureEvents(...)` before publishing through a generated event facade.
Assert the capture record's decoded `payload` and metadata instead of subscribing
to raw NATS subjects or relying only on outbox rows.

Use `service.createSqlOutbox(...)` when a service-local SQL transaction and event
enqueue must commit or roll back together. Configure it once during startup with
a generic SQL `executor` for dispatcher work and a `transaction` runner that
provides the service transaction object plus a transaction-scoped Trellis
`SqlExecutor`. The outbox object is a plain dependency that handlers close over.

```ts
import {
  type SqlExecutor,
  type TrellisServiceSqlOutboxOptions,
} from "@qlever-llc/trellis/service";
import { Result } from "@qlever-llc/trellis";

const sqlOutbox: TrellisServiceSqlOutboxOptions<AppTransaction> = {
  dialect: "postgres",
  executor: poolExecutor,
  transaction: async (work) =>
    pool.transaction(async (tx) =>
      work({ tx, executor: createTransactionExecutor(tx) })
    ),
};

function createTransactionExecutor(tx: AppTransaction): SqlExecutor {
  return {
    query: (statement, params) => tx.query(statement, params),
    execute: async (statement, params) => {
      await tx.execute(statement, params);
    },
  };
}

const outbox = service.createSqlOutbox(sqlOutbox);
const deps = { ordersRepo, auditRepo, outbox };

await service.handle.rpc.orders.ship(async ({ input }) => {
  await deps.outbox.transaction(async ({ tx, event, job }) => {
    await deps.ordersRepo.markShipped(tx, input.orderId);
    await deps.auditRepo.insert(tx, { entityId: input.orderId });

    await event.orders.shipped.enqueue({
      orderId: input.orderId,
      customerId: input.customerId,
      shippedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    }).orThrow();
    await event.audit.recorded.enqueue({
      entityId: input.orderId,
      action: "order.shipped",
    }).orThrow();

    await job.syncCustomer.create({
      customerId: input.customerId,
    }).orThrow();
  }).orThrow();

  return Result.ok({ accepted: true });
});
```

Rules for agents:

- close over the outbox object as a plain dependency when handlers need
  transactional enqueue; handlers do not receive `outbox` as an injected argument
- wrap all service DB writes, event enqueues, and job submission intents that
  must be atomic in `outbox.transaction(...)`
- use transaction-scoped `event.*.*.enqueue(...)` and `job.*.*.create/submit(...)`
  only inside that callback; normal event facades expose `prepare`, `publish`,
  and `listen`, not `enqueue`
- multiple DB writes, event enqueues, and job submissions in one transaction are supported
- do not generate ad hoc local outbox wrappers, manual `SqlOutboxRepository` /
  `OutboxDispatcher` handler wiring, or per-handler Drizzle transaction wrappers

Trellis owns SQL helper-table migration artifacts. Services choose table names
and run the artifacts through their normal database migration tool:

```ts
import { getSqlOutboxMigrations } from "@qlever-llc/trellis/service";

const migrations = getSqlOutboxMigrations({
  dialect: "postgres",
  tables: { outbox: "trellis_outbox", inbox: "trellis_inbox" },
});

for (const migration of migrations) {
  await migrationRunner.register({
    id: migration.id,
    checksum: migration.checksum,
    up: migration.up,
    down: migration.down ?? [],
  });
}
```

Drizzle remains optional through `@qlever-llc/trellis/service/drizzle` adapter
helpers. There is intentionally no direct `createSqlOutbox({ drizzle })` sugar.
If a service uses Drizzle, adapt it into the generic `executor` and `transaction`
options at startup; treat `createDrizzleSqlExecutor(...)` as advanced/adapter
usage, not a normal per-handler pattern.

Use `SqlInboxRepository` only when replaying a message would repeat a
non-idempotent side effect. Register the listener during service startup, not
inside a handler.

Use `NatsKvOutboxRepository` and `NatsKvInboxRepository` for services that do not
have SQL state. They are durable helpers, but they are not atomic with unrelated
database transactions.

## Durable event consumers

Direct `uses.events.subscribe` grants only live or ephemeral listening. A service
that needs replay, ordered processing, or a durable cursor must declare a
top-level `eventConsumers` group in its contract and register the startup
listener with that group. `eventConsumers.<group>.uses` selects dependency events
by top-level `uses.required` or `uses.optional` alias;
`eventConsumers.<group>.self` selects events owned by the same contract.

```ts
const contract = defineServiceContract({ schemas }, () => ({
  id: "shipment-projection@v1",
  apiId: "shipment-projection@v1",
  apiVersion: "1.0.0",
  displayName: "Shipment Projection",
  description: "Projects shipment events into local state.",
  uses: {
    required: {
      orders: orders.use({
        events: { subscribe: ["Orders.Shipped"] },
      }),
    },
  },
  eventConsumers: {
    shipmentProjection: {
      uses: {
        orders: ["Orders.Shipped"],
      },
      replay: "new",
      ordering: "strict",
    },
  },
}));

await service.event.orders.shipped.listen(handleShipment, {}, {
  group: "shipmentProjection",
}).orThrow();
```

Strict groups are globally single-in-flight. For independent messages, declare
`ordering: "parallel"` and pass a positive per-instance `concurrency` to every
listener registration in that group. Registrations in one group must agree.

Dependency durable consumption remains authority-backed by the top-level `uses`
subscription. For durable self-consumption of events owned by the same service,
use `self: ["Entity.Observation"]`. Runtime durable consumers are
Trellis-provisioned only; service code should not create or name arbitrary
JetStream durable consumers.

## Verification

Use the format, typecheck, lint, test, run, and migration commands configured by
the service repository. If contract artifacts or generated SDKs changed, run
`trellis install` and commit `trellis.lock`; `.trellis` output remains disposable.
